divergence_note: A follows an oblique side-by-side apparatus through valve, condition, supported trial, feedback and target macro cuts. B starts from a vertically paired comparison, then cuts frontally into the virtual chamber and uses a downward supported trial view before restoring the complete planned comparison. Neither repeats a permanent exploded wireframe or looping gas dots.

captions.text: Before a gas valve opens, a virtual experiment could run.
Rice plans an AI powered materials laboratory in Houston.
Its digital twin would model temperature, pressure, gas flow and chemical composition.
Researchers could simulate a trial before using physical equipment.
Results would teach the AI what to recommend next.
When uncertain, it would consult a researcher.
The targets include diamond thin films.
NSF backed the project in July.

action_proposals.visible_action: A solid translucent model of the conserved generic chamber receives a broad finite input front. Full-surface heat, large qualitative pressure controls and a second model mixture change distinctly before a supported virtual sample trial. Hypothetical feedback arrives and holds before the next proposed setting; an enlarged uncertainty question reaches pending researcher review.
action_proposals.consequence: Researchers could inspect modeled inputs and a proposed trial before physical use. Future result feedback could inform recommendations and uncertainty could return to researcher judgment; no physical operation or scientific success is depicted.
action_proposals.limits: Original generic apparatus and qualitative planned-research illustration, not an actual Rice machine, interface, numerical model output, synthesis process, grown film, measured material property, actual approval or mandatory hardware interlock. The researcher review destination is an abstract editorial node.
action_proposals.source_basis: Rice states that a digital twin will simulate experiments before physical equipment, learn from results and consult researchers when uncertain.
